scope: First real legacy-Viva to native-Herdr live inheritance at the native default entry. A feature-enabled bare `viva` starts the native host; when a live legacy `viva server` owns the same VIVA_HOME, the native host receives protocol-2 handoff entries with no early ACK, adopts every PTY master into a Herdr session built from the persisted SceneBook, and only then acknowledges so the old host exits. This is a DEGRADED IMPORT, not a lossless takeover, not member execution, not agent/terminal control, not Linux/x86_64 packaging acceptance, and not a released or merged product. The legacy UI remains reachable as `viva workbench`; legacy control commands (`status`, `shutdown`, `dispatch`) still refuse behind a native host.
existing_capability_and_gap: Reused the existing legacy handoff protocol 2 (`send_entries`/`receive_entries`, `acknowledge_prepared`, one PTY master fd per terminal over SCM_RIGHTS), the legacy `Client::connect`/`ServerRestart` control path, the persisted `workbench_layout` SceneBook, and Herdr's existing `App::new_from_handoff` + `ImportedHandoffRuntime` + `HandoffRuntimeState` adoption machinery. The gap was that the native host had no handoff receiver, no mapping from a legacy SceneBook/manifest to a Herdr SessionSnapshot, and bare `viva` either refused or started an empty native session instead of inheriting the only live session.
behavior: With the `herdr-runtime` feature, bare `viva` runs the native runtime. `viva runtime server` checks legacy control sockets (`server.sock`, `resume.sock`, `resume-next.sock`); when one exists and answers, it reads the persisted SceneBook BEFORE asking for a handover, sends `ServerRestart`, connects to the returned handoff socket, and takes the manifest plus one fd per terminal with no acknowledgement. `build_plan` maps scenes to workspaces and tabs to tabs, keeps orphan pane terminals in a trailing restored tab, and deduplicates a terminal placed twice (first placement wins). `build_snapshot` gives consecutive pane ids from 1, stable workspace ids `ws-legacy-N`, carries scene/tab custom names, tab order and active tab, rows/cols, child pid and any ANSI screen/scrollback, uses even horizontal splits with ratio 0.5, and assumes 8x16 px cells. Bootstrap builds a `SessionSnapshot` plus `HashMap<u32, ImportedHandoffRuntime>` and calls `App::new_from_handoff`; it acknowledges ONLY after both sockets bound and `embedding::server_ready()` succeeded, then assumes handoff ownership and unpauses readers. Before that point every error drops the owned fds and the `LegacyConfirm` without acknowledging, so the old host reattaches its readers and keeps serving. If the ACK write itself fails, the code probes the old host: if it still answers it aborts (the old host keeps the sessions); if it is gone it records `native_legacy_handoff_ack_unconfirmed` and keeps the adopted fds. A socket file is treated as stale only when every existing legacy control socket refuses connections; a live or wedged host still blocks a fresh native start, and a stale file is left in place for a later legacy entry.
preserved: live child process and its PID (the adopted pane still owns the original shell)
ANSI screen and scrollback when the legacy entry carries them
confirmed member execution attribution/task/member/grant bindings for adopted live executions (synthetic native binding without a native credential)
not_preserved: legacy terminal ids (new pane numbers are assigned)
pane cwd (every imported pane starts at the native host's current directory)
split ratios, focus and zoom (flattened to even horizontal splits, first pane focused)
agent state and worktree space metadata

boundaries: This is a degraded import, not seamless or lossless: pane cwd, split ratios/focus/zoom, cell pixel size, terminal ids, pane purpose, agent state and worktree space are lost. Do not describe the takeover as preserving the workbench layout.

Ownership is preserved only for the child processes: the old host retires after ACK, the new host owns the duplicated PTY masters, and the child shell PID does not change. Shell state, foreground job state and terminal modes are whatever the ANSI/recent screen restores.

The native host is Unix-only for this path; Windows is not supported. The receiver, fd transfer and adoption tests were executed on macOS aarch64 only. Linux is compiled through the same unix module but was not executed.

ACK ordering is enforced by structure: `receive_from_live_host` takes no ACK, `LegacyConfirm` is the only ACK handle and is consumed after adoption/endpoints. A failed ACK with a still-answering old host aborts and drops the adopted fds; a failed ACK after the old host disappeared is kept and recorded as unconfirmed, because those fds are then the only live copies.
A stale legacy socket is ignored only when every existing legacy control socket refuses a connection; a live or wedged host still blocks the native start. Stale files are not deleted.

The release workflow was updated to build with `--features herdr-runtime`, hash-pin Zig 0.16.0, add NOTICE/SBOM/herdr license and smoke `runtime --version`; the workflow itself was NOT executed (no tag, no release, no publication). Local release smoke covers the aarch64 macOS host build only.

`viva update` now detects a running native host and tells the user to terminate it; no in-place native host takeover/restart was implemented or tested. Legacy `viva status`/`shutdown`/`dispatch` refuse behind a native host and do not silently fall back.
All real takeover tests used task-created HOME/VIVA_HOME fixtures under /tmp. The user's real ~/.viva was not touched. No merge, approval, version bump, tag, npm publish or release occurred.
Independent QA and Haisu's MacBook Air installation/manual UI acceptance remain pending and are not replaced by these checks.

Adopted legacy executions are only requested/running executions with a confirmed launch intent, a persisted launch spec, a named terminal carried by the handoff, a positive PID and a member/automation grant origin; PID equality between the canonical intent and the live pane child is required. They receive a synthetic native binding with an empty credential id, so no native worker credential is revoked on exit. A requested, unconfirmed, unmapped or PID-mismatched execution aborts the takeover before any fd is requested, with the old host still serving.
Native host crash/restart does not reconcile persisted requested/running executions; the owner gate keeps refusing them until a legacy host (via `viva workbench`) or a new adoption path owns them.

The owner capability is still a 0600 same-UID file. The lineage refusal (host descendants and descendants of host-owned executions) is an authenticate-time check, not an OS sandbox. It does NOT cover an independent same-UID process or a worker that reparents itself out of the host ancestry: such a process can read owner-channel.json and authenticate as the owner; this was reproduced at 28f8552. Closing it requires an OS/user-presence trust anchor (for example a Keychain/login-keychain gate) or binding owner auth to the TUI process, which would break the detach/reattach flow unless a new anchor is designed. This is an OPEN owner decision and a blocker for enabling the native entry as the released default; this PR does not close it and must not be described as if it did. Same-UID read of pane.list/pane.read/pane.process_info is observation by design and mutates nothing; dispatch/stop/pause remain owner-gated for callers that cannot present the capability.

qa_fix: Independent QA on head 1257b37 reported four findings; all four were judged correct and fixed. (1) BLOCKER: a same-UID member execution sharing VIVA_HOME could read the 0600 runtime/workbench/owner-channel.json and run `viva runtime host pause` successfully. (2) IMPORTANT: when the live legacy host had a requested/running execution, the native host logged the inheritance line and then exited after the owner gate refused unowned work, leaving the old host serving. (3) MINOR: pane.list/pane.read/pane.process_info are unauthenticated same-UID observation. (4) MINOR: the member-ingress source-hash bundle was stale. This commit refuses owner authentication for host descendants and for descendants of any execution this host owns (audited as native_owner_auth_refused with peer_is_host_descendant / peer_is_execution_descendant), preflights canonical active executions before requesting fds and adopts every confirmed one onto its planned pane with a synthetic binding that carries no native worker credential, documents the pane-observation boundary in README, and annotates/regenerates the member-ingress hash bundle. Pre-fix logs were produced from a clean 1257b37 archive with only the new test files applied. Round 2 on 28f8552 confirmed the descendant fixes but showed the original precise trigger still works: an independent same-UID process that is neither a host nor an execution descendant can read owner-channel.json and pause the host. That residual is NOT fixed and is not claimed fixed; it is recorded as an owner-decision product limitation (see boundaries).
